title: Automating Citrus Budwood Processing for Downstream Pathogen Detection Through Instrument Engineering
protocol: Send Technology Evolving Solutions a spreadsheet of tree information for them to load into their web server.
Use the phone app TES tracker to select a tree.
Hold an NFC collar tag to the phone to load the tree information to the tag.
Insert three to four citrus budwood samples into the BTE-compatible plastic bag carrier.
Close the lid with the plastic bag carrier.
Ensure that the length of the budwood does not exceed 8 inches and is not less than 5 inches.
If the length exceeds 8 inches, use a sterile disposable razor blade or pruning shears decontaminated with 10% bleach solution to shorten it.
If the length is less than 5 inches, collect a different budwood sample to put into the bag.
Remove any axillary growth or large thorns by hand or using 10% bleach-sanitized cutting tools.
Ensure that there are no budwood samples with curved features.
If budwood has curved features, remove them using 10% bleach-sanitized cutting tools and place only the straight portions in the BTE bags.
Use the phone app TES tracker to scan the NFC collar tag of the tree and link it with the NFC clip tag on the sample bag.
Select thicker budwood for stripping the phloem-rich bark inside the BTE chamber, avoiding pulverization of non-phloem-rich tissues.
Place samples into an insulated shipping container with ice packs.
Setup in the fume hood to reduce risk of plant tissue cross-contamination and lab contamination.
Spray the surface of the hood with a 10% sodium hypochlorite solution.
Let the bleach sit for about 1 minute before wiping it off with a paper towel.
Wipe the TE base, weight scale components (scale, air shield, tower), and marker pen with a paper towel sprayed with the bleach solution.
Unwrap a syringe set for the number of samples to be processed.
Place unwrapped syringes inside a covered cardboard box.
Prepare the weight scale.
Remove the weight tower from the scale.
Hold the power button to turn the scale on.
Place the tower on the center of the scale after the scale displays 0.
Slide the weight scale air shield over the front of the scale.
Flip the switch on the back to prepare the tissue extractor base.
Press down the switch on the left side of the box on top.
Wait for a blinking green LED, which indicates that the chamber is ready.
Place 1 L of water in the ultrasonic cleaner.
Wrap two trash bags over the top of the ultrasonic cleaner.
Pour ~5 L of 10% bleach into the ultrasonic cleaner.
Fill the water tub with enough water to submerge a chamber.
Turn on the air compressor and open the valve.
Set up a backdrop to catch the liquid while the chamber is drying.
Load the chamber onto the BTE Base.
Attach an empty sample bag to the back of the chamber.
Use two O-rings to secure the empty bag to the back nozzle of the BTE chamber.
Inspect the blade for signs of wear or damage.
Ensure the arrow on the blade lines up with the single lock symbol.
Ensure the air release on the bottom of the chamber is turned toward the O symbol.
Place the clear lid over the chamber opening.
Slide the clear BTE slide onto the chamber using the track on the right of the chamber.
Push the lock on the bottom of the chamber as far as it can go into the slide.
Mount the plunger cap on the top of the slide.
Place the chamber on the BTE base with the BTE base's nozzle protruding into the back of the chamber.
Wait for the blue LED to blink, indicating successful placement.
Move the white sticker on the NFC clip tag to a Z on the right side of the box.
Move the tag in a slow circular motion until the yellow light starts blinking.
Attach the sample to the BTE base.
Ensure the sample bag has no holes; if there is a hole, patch it with tape.
Place the O-ring over the sample bag to secure it to the front of the BTE nozzle.
Load the unused syringe set onto the weigh scale tower.
Tare the syringe set when the red light begins flashing or the scale displays 0.
Remove the tared syringe set from the weigh scale tower.
Remove the plunger from the syringe with the filter.
Ensure the fluid is in the bottom (non-filter) syringe.
Place the plunger aside on a paper towel or tower where it does not touch any surfaces.
Attach the syringe to the slide exit port by pressing the exit port into the syringe and turning 90°.
Press the top black button to start the machine.
Grab one budwood stick through the bag, and put it through the top of the BTE nozzle.
Grab the budwood stick on the other side of the chamber with the other hand, and slowly inch down into the blade.
Listen for a gentle buzzing sound indicating that the budwood is being stripped of its bark.
Slowly move the budwood back and forth while rotating it.
If a loud, aggressive chopping sound is heard, quickly move the branch to the top.
Press the top button to stop the motor if necessary.
Turn off the motor if no material is coming out of the exit when cutting.
Remove the slide plunger cap and use the plastic of the swab to push the clog out the exit of the machine.
Use the right-side switch to finish processing: Up = Forward cutting; Middle = Motor off; Down = Reverse Cutting.
Press the top black button to stop processing.
Wait for the light to begin flashing yellow again.
Verify the sample weight.
Rotate the syringe 90°, and pull it down to detach.
Place the plunger back on the syringe, and place the syringe on the tower.
Remove some of the sample material if the weight is too high (>0.30 g).
Repeat step 4.4 if the sample weight is too low (<0.20 g).
Homogenize the budwood sample by removing the plunger from the syringe with the sample.
Push the fluid into the syringe with the sample and re-add the plunger.
The plunger pushes the buffer and plant sap through the mesh filter (withholding any large bark tissue pieces) and via the rubber tubing into the empty syringe.
Push the buffer and plant sap back and forth from one syringe to the other.
Repeat mixing process approximately 3-4 times until sample is homogeneous green liquid mixture.
Expel the well-homogenized plant sap sample into a 2 mL sterile microcentrifuge tube without mesh filter.
Store the plant sap sample at -20°C for further use.
Label the sample with bag number using permanent marker.
Disassemble the BTE chamber to clean all possible contaminants.
Remove the clear plastic cover from the chamber.
Clear the chamber slide.
Clear the clog port on the chamber slide.
Turn the air release valve on the bottom of the chamber to the open position.
Place the chamber components into the ultrasonic cleaner.
Place the lid under the chamber to prevent it from floating.
Run the ultrasonic cleaner for 15 min.
Rinse the chamber components in a water bath for at least 30 s.
Move the chamber components to the drying station.
Position the air gun in line with the groove of the upper opening of the chamber.
Press the trigger of the air gun to dispense air for about 30 s.
Position the air gun toward the top nozzles of the chamber.
Press the trigger of the air gun, and slowly trace three full circles around each nozzle entrance.
Position the air gun in the center of the BTE.
Hold the trigger down and move the air gun until it points toward where the slide would be.
Run an air gun over the entire chamber front and back to remove surface water.
Dry the BTE slide.
Position the air gun into the plunger slot of the slide.
Press the trigger to eject water out of the slide exit.
Run an air gun along the interior surface of the slide to dry it.
Run an air gun along the slide groove to push out water.
Quickly run air over the entire exterior of the BTE to remove surface water.
Dry the components.
Hold the slide plunger cap and O-rings in hand.
Press the trigger to run an air gun over the interior surface of the lid.
Place the components in the chamber or slide for continued drying or reassemble them.
Prepare budwood samples for tissue processing as per the regulatorily approved method.
Carry out hand peeling and chopping of the bark tissue.
Perform freeze-drying of the chopped bark tissue.
Pulverize the freeze-dried bark tissue.
Centrifuge the pulverized bark tissue to separate plant sap.
Transfer the plant sap to the RNA extraction tube.
Extract RNA from plant sap obtained using the current laboratory procedure.
Purify the extracted RNA using a semi-automated magnetic bead-based method.
Measure the concentration of the purified RNA at an OD wavelength of 260 nm.
Assess the purity of the RNA by measuring the OD ratio of 260/280.
Check the integrity of the RNA using RT-qPCR targeting NADH dehydrogenase citrus gene mRNA.
Prepare all non-infected citrus budwood samples (1-72) in BTE carrier bags.
Prepare an equal number (72) of samples in the two-syringe BTE sample collection system, with one syringe for each sample.
Separate the 72 carrier bags and syringes into six batches (I-VI), each containing 12 samples.
Process Batch I/Samples 1-12 using chamber A.
Sanitize chamber A after processing sample 12.
Process Batch II/Samples 13-24 using chamber B.
Sanitize chamber B after processing sample 24.
Process Batch III/Samples 25-36 using chamber C.
Sanitize chamber C after processing sample 36.
Process Batch IV/Samples 37-48 using the sanitized chamber A.
Process Batch V/Samples 49-60 using the sanitized chamber B.
Process Batch VI/Samples 61-72 using the sanitized chamber C.
Store all BTE carrier bags containing samples at 4°C until further use.
Extract and purify RNA from the 72 plant sap samples using a semi-automated magnetic bead-based method.
Perform RT-qPCR for the detection of citrus viruses and viroids as previously described.
Prepare three BTE chambers.
Prepare two mix-infected citrus budwood samples in separate BTE carrier bags.
Gather 70 non-infected citrus budwood samples from previous steps.
Replace Sample 3-Batch I and Sample 51-Batch V with the infected samples.
Combine the 72 carrier bags into six batches of 12 samples each.
Prepare a double-syringe system for each sample.
Initiate BTE citrus budwood tissue processing following the specified sequence.
Extract RNA from the 72 plant sap samples as per protocol steps.
Perform RT-qPCR to detect citrus viruses and viroids.
